description: The main session's final record for a run: which stages ran, whether each gate passed, what it cost, and the verdict. A passing pass_record for HEAD is what lets a push through.

commit.description: The commit the run was for.

row.description: The matrix row the run followed (for example code.M).

record.description: Path of the stage's record, relative to the repository root.

gate.description: The stage's gate, or null when it has none.

rounds.description: How many rounds the stage took.

tokens.description: Token usage of the run. by_model maps a model name to {output, fresh_input, cache_read, output_lower_bound}, each an integer count: what the stage agents spent. output_lower_bound is how many messages never got their final usage entry: when it is above 0, output is at least the count given. orchestration, present when the orchestrator ran the run in legs, holds the same counts for the legs' own transcripts, per model and apart from by_model.

open_findings.description: What the run leaves open: the surviving non-blocking findings of every review stage, each with the stage it came from. `pass` fills it from the merged review records, so that it outlasts the run's review files. Absent from a pass record written before 0.5.0.

stage.description: The review stage the finding came from.

severity.description: A finding that survives with BLOCKING fails its gate, so a passed run holds only MAJOR and MINOR ones.

claim.description: What is wrong, in one sentence.

failure_scenario.description: A concrete input or sequence of events that goes wrong: a follow-up fix run takes it as its bug report.

gaps.description: What the detective found missing, from every review stage that has a detective, each with the stage it came from. Absent from a pass record written before 0.5.0.

stage.description: The review stage the gap came from.

ac.description: The acceptance criterion the gap concerns, or null.
